De Montfort Road.note: 1970s close of red/orange brick two- and three-storey flats and town houses with dark-stained boarding, green-door garage courts, tall beech hedges and shrubbery that hide most buildings.

Christchurch Bridge.note: Only one view loaded: 1990s three-storey orange-red brick flat blocks with gables and brick bands, a brick bin store, and houses beyond; hedges along the far side.

Wolsey Road.note: North end is Victorian/Edwardian red-brick semis and short terraces with bays and slate roofs, some rendered; south end has 1970s-80s brown/orange brick houses with tile roofs behind fences and big hedges.

Thames Side.note: 1980s close of red-brick two-storey starter homes and three-storey brick flats with green garage doors, open-plan lawns and shrubs and a parking court.

Caversham Road.note: Caversham centre: shops with flats over

St Martins Precinct.note: Paved pedestrian shopping precinct with trees and red market parasols, lined by two-storey buff-brick 1960s/70s shop blocks with continuous glazed shopfronts and grey fascia bands; both views are a user photosphere.

George Street.note: Mixed: Victorian two-storey terraces (red brick and painted white/cream) near the Gosbrook Road lights, a single-storey red-brick hall with slate roof, a three-storey 1950s buff-brick flats block and open land; the south view is central Reading with a high-rise tower and offices, not Caversham.

Church Street.note: Historic main street: Georgian red-brick house with sash windows and arched window, a 1980s red-brick mansard office, white-painted pub and cream low cottages with clay tile roofs, a gabled grey-brick Victorian corner block, and long red-brick garden walls under trees.

Vastern Road.note: Only a riverside towpath photosphere: a stepped 1980s red-brick terrace with dark sawtooth roofs and dark-framed glazed balconies, behind hedges; other view is just the river.

Peppard Road.note: A long tree-lined main road: many stretches are just woodland or hedge, with interwar semis (some mock-Tudor gables, rendered upper floors), a red-brick Victorian lodge, modern red-brick detached houses and a few bungalows set well back behind hedges and fences.

All Hallows Road.note: large 1920s-30s detached (Peppard Road, the Heights): mock-Tudor gables, render, tile

Promenade Road.note: Four-storey 1990s-2000s red-brick flat blocks with white window bands and balconies set in lawns behind hedges and railings; second view is mostly hedge and trees.

Abbotsmead Place.note: Modern three/four-storey retirement-style flats in red brick and white render with steep gables, behind brick piers and shrubs; the other view is solid trees.

Thames Side Promenade.note: Views are from Church Road at the corner of Buckside: Edwardian red-brick and white-rendered buildings with gables, a mock-Tudor corner cafe and a long red-brick boundary wall; a later red-brick house with dormers on the corner.

Brigham Road.note: 1980s close of red-brick two-storey starter homes and three-storey brick flats with green garage doors, open-plan lawns and shrubs and a parking court.

Kingfisher Place.note: Only a riverside towpath photosphere: a stepped 1980s red-brick terrace with dark sawtooth roofs and dark-framed glazed balconies, behind hedges; other view is just the river.

King's Meadow Road.note: Riverside commercial area: a tall modern block of flats with dark grey ground floor and orange/brick-clad upper storeys behind lawn and columnar trees, and a red-brick 1980s office building on a grassy bank; flat roofs. (Roofs are flat; grey_tile used as the nearest option.)

Norman Place.note: Only a riverside towpath photosphere: a stepped 1980s red-brick terrace with dark sawtooth roofs and dark-framed glazed balconies, behind hedges; other view is just the river.

South View Avenue.note: Mixed street of Edwardian red-brick semis and short terraces with slate roofs and bay windows, some interwar semis, a modern three-storey brick townhouse block and a 1960s-70s house; a red-brick Victorian church (St Anne's area) at the west end; small front gardens behind low brick walls.

Bristow Court.note: 1980s two-storey red-brick sheltered flats with some white rendered gables behind a low red-brick wall and lawn, and a red-brick house beside a car park/service yard.

Gosbrook Road.note: Long Victorian red-brick terraces (some painted white/cream) with slate roofs and small walled front yards, a red-brick Victorian chapel and a few modern brick flats; the west end opens onto the meadows park.

Harley Road.note: 1980s two-storey red-brick sheltered flats with some white rendered gables behind a low red-brick wall and lawn, and a red-brick house beside a car park/service yard.

Elliotts Way.note: 1990s estate of orange-red brick terraces, semis and detached houses with porch canopies and contrasting brick bands, plus three-storey brick flat blocks with garages; open-plan fronts and paved parking.

Cardinal Close.note: 1970s close of red/orange brick two- and three-storey flats and town houses with dark-stained boarding, green-door garage courts, tall beech hedges and shrubbery that hide most buildings.

The Willows.note: 1980s estate of red-brick two-storey semis, short terraces and detached houses with small gabled porch canopies, garages and open-plan paved fronts and shrubs.

Patrick Road.note: Mixed street: three-storey modern red-brick townhouses with integral garages behind hedges at the south end, Victorian red-brick bay-fronted terraces and white-rendered cottages with low white walls at the north end; one view mostly fence and trees.

Tamesis Place.note: Only one view loaded: 1990s three-storey orange-red brick flat blocks with gables and brick bands, a brick bin store, and houses beyond; hedges along the far side.

Claydon Court.note: 1980s close of red-brick two-storey starter homes and three-storey brick flats with green garage doors, open-plan lawns and shrubs and a parking court.

School Lane.note: A mix: four-storey 1960s red-brick council flats with blue window panels set in lawns, 1980s/90s red-brick houses and a small hipped-roof flats block, and postwar semis behind picket fences further along.

St Stephens Close.note: 1980s close of red-brick two-storey starter homes and three-storey brick flats with green garage doors, open-plan lawns and shrubs and a parking court.

Crendon Court.note: Only one view loaded and it resolves to The Willows: 1980s red-brick two-storey houses and a three-storey red-brick flat block with shrubs; may not show Crendon Court itself.

Heron Island.note: 1980s riverside townhouses and flats on an island in the Thames: three-storey red and yellow-buff brick with integral garages and full-height black-and-white mock-Tudor bay windows/gables, dark tile roofs, block paving and willow trees.

King's Road.note: Unbroken Victorian/Edwardian two-storey terraces, red brick with buff and grey dressings and gabled bays, some painted white or cream and one buff-brick pair, all slate roofs and tiny front yards behind low walls.

Queen's Road.note: Tight Victorian two-storey terraces in red brick with polychrome (buff/grey) brick dressings, bay windows and slate roofs, a few painted white or cream, behind tiny front yards with low brick walls; one modern three-storey brick flats block.

Coldicutt Street.note: Mixed: Victorian red-brick terraces with stuccoed bay windows and arched doorways (some painted white) behind low walls and railings, modern flats with red-brick ground floors and grey-buff brick upper floors with balconies, and 1980s-90s red-brick flats with forecourt parking.

Mill Road.note: Red-brick Victorian terraces with slate roofs and some painted or slate-hung frontages, a car-repair yard and a 1950s brick semi; the south end opens onto trees and a footpath.

Piggotts Road.note: Victorian two-storey terraced cottages in red brick alternating with white and cream painted fronts, slate roofs and tall chimneys, tiny front gardens behind low walls; also 1950s-60s brick semis with brown tile roofs and forecourt parking.

Mill Green.note: 1930s red-brick and rendered semis with hipped tile roofs, a three-storey dark-brick flat block, and the brick-walled entrance to the Heron Island development; big trees overhang the road.

Champion Road.note: Victorian red-brick cottages and a tall old brick wall with flint panels and an arched green door, a white-rendered pair of cottages with slate roofs set at the back of the pavement, and small gravel yards; mature trees behind walls.

Forge Close.note: Modern three-storey townhouses: a 2010s red-brick terrace with slate roof, dormers and Juliet balconies, and a 1980s-90s three-storey terrace with brick ground floor and white-painted upper floors; brick boundary walls and shrubs.

Send Road.note: Back-land lane: new three-storey buff-brick townhouses with dormers under construction behind hoardings, a parking court with older brick housing and a low flat-roofed building beyond. Further along it is a narrow lane of 1960s-70s brick detached houses and chalet bungalows with brick front walls and forecourt parking.

The Causeway.note: Half light-industrial (brick warehouses and clad workshop/offices with yards) and half housing: 1960s-70s red-brick semis with white-painted lower panels and garages, plus a Victorian red-brick cottage terrace with dark tile roofs.

Monkley Court.note: A 1960s three-storey red-brick block of flats with balconies set behind hedges, facing a row of Victorian red-brick and white-painted cottages with slate roofs and tall chimneys right on the pavement; large trees around.

Star Road.note: A real mix: Victorian silver-grey (Reading) brick terraces with red brick dressings, bays and slate roofs; a three-storey 1950s-60s flats block with pale brick and rendered panels; 1970s red-brick townhouses with integral garages; postwar red-brick semis; short front gardens behind low brick walls.

Brook Lea.note: Back-land lane: new three-storey buff-brick townhouses with dormers under construction behind hoardings, a parking court with older brick housing and a low flat-roofed building beyond. Further along it is a narrow lane of 1960s-70s brick detached houses and chalet bungalows with brick front walls and forecourt parking.

Paddock Road.note: Half light-industrial (brick warehouses and clad workshop/offices with yards) and half housing: 1960s-70s red-brick semis with white-painted lower panels and garages, plus a Victorian red-brick cottage terrace with dark tile roofs.

Deans Farm.note: Half light-industrial (brick warehouses and clad workshop/offices with yards) and half housing: 1960s-70s red-brick semis with white-painted lower panels and garages, plus a Victorian red-brick cottage terrace with dark tile roofs.

Talbot Close.note: 1960s-70s terraces in buff/yellow-brown brick with white weatherboard or painted panels on the upper floor, a continuous tiled canopy over the front doors and garages, shallow concrete-tile roofs; open lawns and grass verges with trees.

Amersham Road.note: Post-war/1970s council-style estate road: two-storey red-brick terraces with shallow brown concrete-tile roofs and flat porches, newer orange-brick flats and houses, one bungalow; lots of trees, hedges and open green space break up the frontage.

Briant's Avenue.note: 1930s semis and detached houses in red brick, some with cream-rendered upper floors and hipped tiled roofs, paved front drives; a small parade of two shops in converted semis near the north end. Near the south end a 1990s orange-red brick block of flats with a car park behind a brick wall.

Mead Close.note: 2000s housing-association estate: three/four-storey red-brick flat blocks with dark timber-clad and white-panelled balcony bays, plus two-storey red-brick terraces, round a communal lawn with young trees and car parking.

Dickens Close.note: 1990s-2000s three-storey townhouses with integral garages: buff-brick lower floors and white-rendered top floors with small gables, Juliet balconies; lots of trees and hedges and a garage block.

Caleta Close.note: 1970s estate of two-storey brown/red-brick terraces with shallow tile roofs and small porch canopies, facing a big open green with mature trees; timber fences and garage blocks.

Douglas Road.note: 1960s-70s estate of semis and short terraces in red or brown-buff brick with white-painted or dark-panelled bands between the windows, shallow concrete-tile roofs, integral garages; open-plan lawns and grass verges.

Henley Road.note: Interwar semis and detached houses set well back behind hedges, trees and front drives, many with white-rendered upper floors and some mock-Tudor gables over red-brick ground floors; leafy and suburban, often hidden by planting.

Clonmel Close.note: Late-1990s/2000s developer estate: two-storey houses and coach houses (flats over garages) in orange-red and yellow-buff brick with contrasting brick bands, some tile-hung gables, brown concrete-tile roofs, small open lawns and drives; a 3-4 storey flats block at the edge.

Ruskin.note: 2000s three- and four-storey blocks of flats in orange-buff and red brick with dormer windows, small gabled porch canopies and dark tile roofs, set around parking courts with hedges and mature trees on the boundary.

Lower Henley Road.note: 1930s red-brick semis with hipped orange clay tile roofs set back behind wide grass verges, hedges and service roads; a later short terrace with dormers at the Henley Road junction; very green, houses often hidden by planting.

Luscombe Close.note: Late-1960s/70s estate of two-storey terraces and maisonette blocks: buff and orange brick ground floors with orange tile-hung or dark-boarded upper floors, shallow brown concrete-tile roofs, flat canopy porches, open lawns.

Flambards.note: 1980s-90s red/orange-brick three-storey flat block and two-storey houses with dark tile roofs and small tiled porch canopies, shrub beds and big trees; a tall leylandii hedge lines the entrance.

Meadow Way.note: 2000s development of three- and four-storey red-brick flat blocks and townhouses with dark-stained timber cladding panels, white-framed balconies, dormers and an archway through to rear parking; dark tile roofs, hedged shrub beds and lots of trees.

Peel Close.note: 1970s estate of two-storey brown/red-brick terraces with shallow tile roofs and small porch canopies, facing a big open green with mature trees; timber fences and garage blocks.

Eccles Close.note: 1960s-70s estate: two-storey red/brown-brick terraces and semis with white-painted panels between the windows, shallow concrete-tile roofs, set round an open communal lawn with footpaths; close-boarded fences at the sides.

The Slopes.note: 1980s-90s red/orange-brick three-storey flat block and two-storey houses with dark tile roofs and small tiled porch canopies, shrub beds and big trees; a tall leylandii hedge lines the entrance.

Alston Walk.note: 1970s estate of plain two-storey red-brick terraces with shallow-pitched or near-flat roofs and simple flat porch canopies, plus a newer pair of 1990s red/buff-brick terraces with gabled porches; open grass and paved frontages.

Ian Mikardo Way.note: 1980s-90s housing-association style estate: two-storey red/orange brick terraces, semis and small flat blocks with brown concrete-tile roofs, little tiled porch canopies, some solar panels, open lawns and parking courts.

Charles Evans Way.note: 1970s estate of long two-storey red-brick terraces with shallow pitched roofs, often seen from the back over close-boarded fences; parking courts, grass corners and a few trees.

Managua Close.note: 1980s-90s close of yellow-buff and red-brick two-storey houses and small flat blocks with a few brick bungalows, dark/brown concrete-tile roofs, open-plan lawns and young trees.

Nire Road.note: 1980s-90s housing estate of yellow-buff and red-brick two-storey houses and small flat blocks with brown/dark concrete-tile roofs, small gabled porch canopies, open lawns and lots of hedges and young trees.

Rhine Close.note: Late-1980s/90s housing-association style close: two-storey red and orange-brick semis and short terraces with brown tile roofs and small tiled porch canopies, block-paved parking courts, grass and young trees.

Honey Meadow Close.note: 1980s-90s close of two-storey yellow-buff and red-brick terraces and semis with brown/dark concrete-tile roofs, small gabled tiled porch canopies, solar panels on some; open lawns, shrubs and many trees, next to a large open green.

Rothwell Walk.note: 1970s estate terraces of plain red brick with shallow-pitched brown/grey concrete-tile roofs and flat porch canopies, seen mostly from the back with timber garden fences and bins; some later orange-brick 1990s houses nearby.

Nelson Road.note: 1930s white-rendered semis with brick bays and porches, a Victorian red-brick semi with white-painted ground floor, and a 1980s-90s red-brick sheltered/flat block with parking court; low brick walls and hedges.

Anglefield Road.note: 1920s-30s council-built red-brick semis and short terraces of four with hipped orange-red clay tile roofs, tall chimneys and small tiled porch hoods, behind low fences, hedges or open paved drives.

Donkin Hill.note: Mixed: red-brick Victorian terraces with slate roofs and some painted fronts at the bottom, a block of postwar brick flats at the junction, then 1930s red/orange-brick semis with red tile roofs and paved forecourts up the hill; one side open scrub and trees. At the South View Avenue mini-roundabout the corner has an old painted-render shop building and advertising hoardings.

Waleys Place.note: A 1980s-90s detached house with brick ground floor and cream-panelled mock-Tudor upper floor and slate roof, older red-brick houses beyond, and a red-brick Edwardian school with tall windows; low brick walls and a big street tree.

Ardler Road.note: Cream-rendered and pebbledashed interwar semis with arched porches and low brick front walls, plus an older cream-rendered cottage and tall wooden fences; one side is open green with mature trees.

Saint John's Road.note: 1990s-2000s red-brick two-storey terraces and semis with dark tile roofs and tiled porch canopies, small white-rendered gable on one; open forecourt parking, a fenced playground and an industrial shed on the entrance lane.

Marsack Street.note: Victorian terraces and pairs in red brick (one with silver-grey/red patterned brickwork) and white-painted render, slate roofs, bay windows and small front gardens behind low walls, picket fences and hedges; industrial sheds at one end and 1930s semis beyond.

Montague Street.note: A 1980s-90s detached house with brick ground floor and cream-panelled mock-Tudor upper floor and slate roof, older red-brick houses beyond, and a red-brick Edwardian school with tall windows; low brick walls and a big street tree.

Brackstone Close.note: 1990s-2000s red-brick two-storey terraces and semis with dark tile roofs and tiled porch canopies, small white-rendered gable on one; open forecourt parking, a fenced playground and an industrial shed on the entrance lane.

St John's Road.note: Mixed street: modern red-brick semis and terraces with forecourt parking at the north end beside an industrial yard, a Victorian red-brick villa behind a corrugated fence, a gothic flint/brick church with trees, and 1930s brick semis beyond.

Washington Road.note: Red-brick Victorian/Edwardian terraces with bay windows at the south end; further north early-20th-century terraces with pale render/pebbledash upper floors over brick, small paved front gardens behind low walls. A single-storey red-brick school building with blue windows and railings sits on the corner (SCHOOL KEEP CLEAR markings).

Richard Nevill Court.note: 1930s white-rendered semis with brick bays and porches, a Victorian red-brick semi with white-painted ground floor, and a 1980s-90s red-brick sheltered/flat block with parking court; low brick walls and hedges.

Alder Road.note: 1990s-2000s red-brick two-storey houses with dark tile roofs and tiled porch canopies, seen over close-boarded fences, beside a small gated industrial yard; hedges and trees.

Saint John's RoadBanana Moon Day Nursery.note: 1930s white-rendered semis with brick bays and porches, a Victorian red-brick semi with white-painted ground floor, and a 1980s-90s red-brick sheltered/flat block with parking court; low brick walls and hedges.

Hardy Close.note: 1990s-2000s two-storey red-brick terraces with small front gables, some gables and ends white-rendered, dark tile roofs and red doors; low brick walls with steps and paved forecourts, big trees at the entrance.

Marsack street.note: Victorian terraces and pairs in red brick (one with silver-grey/red patterned brickwork) and white-painted render, slate roofs, bay windows and small front gardens behind low walls, picket fences and hedges; industrial sheds at one end and 1930s semis beyond.

Southview Park.note: A small 1970s-80s business park: brick-and-grey-metal-clad two-storey workshop/office units with car parking in front, a brick office block, hedges and a few trees; 1930s houses visible beyond.

Keston Close.note: Mostly side walls and fences seen: a terrace of 1970s light brown/orange-brick houses with concrete-tile roofs behind a long brick garden wall, and tall conifers and fencing opposite.

Cromwell Road.note: Victorian red-brick terraces with white-painted ground-floor bays, contrasting yellow/white brick bands and slate roofs, tiny front gardens behind low red-brick walls; a 1930s semi and a 1990s brick semi near the north end.

Elmleigh Court.note: 1980s close of red-brick detached and link-detached houses with integral garages, many with black-and-white mock-Tudor gables and first floors, tiled canopy porches; open-plan lawns, shrubs and a few conifers.

Coach House Mews.note: 1980s close of red-brick detached and link-detached houses with integral garages, many with black-and-white mock-Tudor gables and first floors, tiled canopy porches; open-plan lawns, shrubs and a few conifers.

Hampden Road.note: Victorian red-brick terraces with white-painted ground-floor bays, contrasting yellow/white brick bands and slate roofs, tiny front gardens behind low red-brick walls; a 1930s semi and a 1990s brick semi near the north end.

Donegal Close.note: 1960s-70s terraces with red-brick ground floors and dark-stained timber or white-painted weatherboard panels on the upper floor, shallow pitched concrete-tile roofs; open lawns, a garage court and mature trees at the entrance.

Fairfax Close.note: 1980s-90s executive cul-de-sac: detached orange-brick houses with brown concrete tile roofs, integral garages, open lawns, hedges and a few trees; one or two have white-painted upper gables.

Rufus Isaacs Road.note: 1990s cul-de-sac of red/orange brick detached houses with integral garages and brown concrete tile roofs, plus a buff brick flat block and big three-storey red brick block; one view black, one mostly a side wall.

Queen Annes Gate.note: 1980s executive estate of detached red-brick houses with garages, about half with black-and-white mock-Tudor upper floors and gables; open-plan lawns, block-paved drives and mature trees.

Waller Court.note: 1990s close of red/orange brick terraced and semi houses with brick bands, small gabled porch canopies (one with mock-Tudor gable) and brown tile roofs, open-plan lawns and parking.

Barclose Avenue.note: Views show Henley Road at the avenue's mouth rather than the avenue: 1920s-30s detached and semi-detached houses, red brick and render, several with black-and-white mock-Tudor gables, behind brick walls and hedges with big trees.

Prospect Street.note: Victorian two- and three-storey terraces fronting the pavement: red brick and painted (white, one blue-painted) cottages to the north, a row of small shops with green and black fascias and awnings near the mini-roundabout, with a big 1980s red-brick mansard block opposite.

South Street.note: Victorian red-brick chapel/church hall with arched windows and slate roof, red-brick and white-painted terraces beyond, a white low building with a red fascia, behind low walls and hedges; one view partly blocked by roadworks barriers.

Short Street.note: Victorian red-brick and buff/stone-faced terraced houses with slate roofs behind low brick walls with piers, plus a 1970s two-storey red-brick flat block set back behind grass.

Westfield Road.note: Long Victorian terraces of red brick with yellow-brick bands, some painted white, with bays, slate roofs and dormers; tiny front gardens behind low walls, hedges and picket fences; south end opens onto trees by the park.

North Street.note: Victorian red-brick terraces with yellow-brick bands and slate roofs, one white-painted, tiny yards behind low walls; other view is a rear alley of brick walls and lock-up garages.

Falkland Road.note: Reading red brick and silver-grey brick with red dressings, some painted; slate; bays; low brick front walls

The Warren.note: A narrow leafy lane where large detached houses are almost entirely hidden behind tall hedges, brick walls, fences and mature trees; wall and roof proportions are guesses from glimpses.

Church Road.note: A busy main road with Victorian red-brick buildings under slate roofs, a 1960s brick flat block, and a black-and-white mock-Tudor house above flint walls and hedges.

Buckside.note: Views are from Church Road at the corner of Buckside: Edwardian red-brick and white-rendered buildings with gables, a mock-Tudor corner cafe and a long red-brick boundary wall; a later red-brick house with dormers on the corner.

Bridge Street.note: Caversham's main shopping street: two- and three-storey Victorian and Edwardian buildings built up to the pavement, mixed red brick, grey brick and painted render, with continuous shopfronts and a busy main road.

Upper Warren Avenue.note: Wooded avenue of large detached houses and bungalows on big plots, almost entirely hidden by hedges, gates and mature trees; a red-tiled bungalow, a cream rendered house and a new orange-brick house were glimpsed.

Graveney Drive.note: A wooded drive with a few 1960s red-brick detached houses on sloping front lawns, the rest hidden by trees and banks.

Ridge Hall Close.note: 1960s-70s close of detached brown and buff brick houses with shallow roofs, uppers hung with red-brown tiles or clad in white boards, flat-roofed garages and porches, and open-plan lawns and block-paved drives.

Lawrence Avenue Mews.note: A Victorian Gothic red-brick lodge with steep gables, stone-mullioned windows and dark tile roofs behind brick gate piers and railings on a low wall; the other view is dense trees.

Boundary Lane.note: A Victorian Gothic red-brick lodge with steep gables, stone-mullioned windows and dark tile roofs behind brick gate piers and railings on a low wall; the other view is dense trees.

Highmoor Road.note: Interwar red-brick detached and semi houses with hipped dark-tile roofs, some white-rendered bays, plus a red-brick church hall and small modern flats block at the west end; tall hedges and close-board fences on low red-brick walls hide many fronts.

St Peter's Avenue.note: Leafy road of detached houses largely hidden by tall hedges and trees: interwar and 1960s-80s red and orange brick houses, some bungalows with brown concrete tile roofs, a few white-rendered upper floors; low brick walls, fences and hedges in front.

Grass Hill.note: A steep, narrow, heavily wooded lane where only glimpses of red-brick and white-painted detached houses show through the trees and hedges.

Kelmscott Close.note: Small close of 1950s-60s red-brick detached houses with white windows, one chalet with a dark tile-hung gable, behind hedges and low brick walls with grass verges and big trees.

Symeon Place.note: 2000s development of three-storey red-brick blocks of flats and townhouses with cream rendered ground floors and bays, balconies and hipped roofs, set in communal lawns with clipped hedges.

St. Peter's Avenue.note: Main road of Edwardian and interwar red-brick houses with bay windows and some black-and-white gables, behind tall hedges and close-board fences, plus a modern orange-brick block and the odd bungalow.

Wychcotes.note: Small 1960s close of brown-brick detached houses and bungalows with low brown roofs among big cedars, hedges and grass banks; little was visible in the two views.

Woodcote Road.note: Main road of Edwardian and interwar red-brick houses with bay windows and some black-and-white gables, behind tall hedges and close-board fences, plus a modern orange-brick block and the odd bungalow.

St. Peter's Hill.note: 2000s development of three-storey red-brick blocks of flats and townhouses with cream rendered ground floors and bays, balconies and hipped roofs, set in communal lawns with clipped hedges.

St Peter's Hill.note: From the main road entrance: modern detached houses with red-brick ground floors and cream-rendered upper floors behind brick gate piers, mostly hidden by dense hedges and trees.

Scolars Close.note: Both views are from St Peter's Hill and show mostly mature trees, close-board fences and hedges; only a couple of distant red-brick houses are visible.

Westonbirt Drive.note: Only one house visible: a 1970s dark-red/brown brick detached house with a dark tile roof and solar panels, set among woodland; the other view is solid vegetation.

Blagrave Lane.note: Rural lane of scattered detached houses and a white-rendered cottage behind fences, fields and trees; houses barely visible, one view blank.

Chazey Road.note: Leafy road of mixed-age detached houses and bungalows, red brick or white/cream render, largely hidden behind tall hedges, brick walls and gates.

Mapledene.note: Large modern red-brick detached houses in Georgian style with brick piers, railings and gates on low walls, along a leafy winding road.

Balliol Road.note: Large red-brick detached houses behind hedges and white picket fences, generous gardens and mature trees.

River Road.note: Big Victorian red-brick villa plus later detached houses and a chalet bungalow along a gravel lane; one view failed, imagery dated 2012.

Hewett Avenue.note: A quiet road mostly walled in by tall hedges, with postwar bungalows behind low brick walls and a few pale-brick 1960s semis on open lawns.

High Meadow.note: Bungalows and chalet bungalows with white-rendered walls and brown tile roofs, seen over tall close-board fences and hedges; few frontages visible.

Hewett Close.note: A small close of buff-brick 1970s chalet bungalows and houses with steep brown tile roofs on open-plan lawns.

Knowle Close.note: A quiet close of long low red-brick bungalows with brown tiled roofs, garages and open lawns, mature trees behind.

Upper Woodcote Road.note: Wide main road with grass verges; detached houses and chalets of mixed age (red brick with white rendered or dark-timbered gables, cream render with red tile roofs, a few interwar semis) set back behind tall hedges and low brick walls.

Little Woodcote Close.note: large 1920s-30s detached (Peppard Road, the Heights): mock-Tudor gables, render, tile

Priory Avenue.note: Edwardian red-brick villas with gables and bays, a mock-Tudor gabled flat block and a red-brick chalet-style cottage with dormers; low red-brick walls with piers and tall fences, one view mostly fence and a skip.

Dovedale Close.note: Red-brick low-rise flats set in communal lawns with trees, plus newer red-brick houses behind fences.

Woodrow Court.note: Mostly shrubs, a wooded bank and a car park; only the corner of a red-brick, tile-hung 1980s-looking flats block is visible.

Clifton Park Road.note: Mix of red-brick semi-bungalows behind fences and older large houses, one with mock-Tudor gables, in a leafy setting; one view failed.

Priest Hill.note: Edwardian red-brick detached houses and semis with gables, many with black-and-white mock-Tudor timbering or white-rendered upper storeys, bay windows and dark plain-tile or slate roofs; Victorian red-brick terraces near the bottom; low brick walls and hedges, many front gardens paved for parking.

Hemdean Rise.note: Late-Victorian/Edwardian red-brick terraces with front gables, two-storey bays, buff/red brick string courses and slate roofs, one terrace in grey Reading brick with red dressings; small front gardens behind low brick walls.

Hemdean Road.note: Long road: the south end is Victorian/Edwardian red brick terraces with slate roofs, bays and low brick front walls (many paved for parking), with Edwardian semis having white-rendered gables; the north end becomes interwar semis with red brick ground floors, white render or pebbledash upstairs, brown tile roofs and hedges.

The Mount.note: Large Edwardian red-brick villas and semis with white-painted bay windows, gables, balconies and tall chimneys behind clipped hedges and low brick walls.

Chester Street.note: Victorian red-brick terraces with white painted bays and slate roofs, plus Edwardian semis with gables and timber detailing, behind low brick walls and hedges; corner shops where it meets Prospect Street.

St Anne's Road.note: Large late-Victorian and Edwardian villas and semis in red brick, some silver-grey Reading brick with red-brick dressings and some painted white, with bays, gables (several with mock-Tudor timbering) and slate or dark tile roofs; low brick walls, hedges and paved drives.

Rectory Road.note: Victorian terraces of red brick and silver-grey Reading brick with red-brick dressings, white-painted bay windows, gabled end houses and slate roofs; small front yards behind low walls.

Hemdean Hill.note: Victorian red-brick terraces and semis with slate roofs, white-painted bay windows and tall chimneys, behind low brick walls; one side has a long old rendered garden wall and garages.

Auburn Court.note: From Church Road: a three-storey 1960s red-brick flats block with white-boarded window bands and hipped roof, plus an old red-brick and flint cottage group with orange clay tile roofs behind flint walls.

Oxford Street.note: Long plain Victorian red-brick terraces with yellow brick bands and lintels, slate roofs and chimneys, front doors up steps behind tiny yards and low brick walls; a modern three-storey red-brick infill at one end.

Caversham House.note: A busy main road with Victorian red-brick buildings under slate roofs, a 1960s brick flat block, and a black-and-white mock-Tudor house above flint walls and hedges.

The Bakehouse.note: Victorian terraces of red brick and silver-grey Reading brick with red-brick dressings, white-painted bay windows, gabled end houses and slate roofs; small front yards behind low walls.

Blossom Road.note: 2000s three-storey red-brick flats with roof dormers and rooflights, white uPVC windows and dark tile roofs, beside parking courts, with red-brick houses beyond.

Copperfields.note: 1980s-90s close of large red-brick detached houses with bay windows and gabled fronts set on open lawns.

Darell Road.note: Large Edwardian red-brick houses with tall chimneys, bays and rendered gables, mostly screened by clipped hedges on low brick walls and big garden trees.

Albert Road.note: Edwardian red-brick detached and semi houses with steep gables, some with white-rendered or mock-Tudor upper gables and buff-brick dressings; a modern red-brick flats block at the south end; thick hedges and low brick walls in front, trees and a green at the north end.

Matlock Road.note: Interwar semis with red-brick ground floors and white rendered upper floors under dark tiled roofs, fronted by hedges, fences and paved drives.

Ilkley Road.note: Mixed interwar detached houses, some white rendered with mock-Tudor gables, some red brick, plus bungalows, mostly behind hedges and close-board fences; few houses were clearly visible.

Buxton Avenue.note: Edwardian to 1920s semis and detached houses with bay windows, red brick below and often white render or roughcast above, behind low brick walls and fences.

Harrogate Road.note: Late-Victorian red-brick villas and semis with slate roofs, white bands or chequered brickwork and tall chimneys along the north side behind low brick walls and hedges; the south side is back-garden fences, garages and St Andrew's church.

Woburn Close.note: 1960s-70s close of orange/buff-brick terraces and link-detached houses, some with tile-hung or boarded upper panels, open frontages and trees at the end.

Richmond Road.note: A quiet road of individually built detached houses and a few bungalows, red brick or white render, mostly screened by tall hedges with grass verges.

Kidmore Road.note: Long leafy road of big Edwardian and interwar red-brick detached and semi houses, many with white-rendered or mock-Tudor gables; deep front gardens behind hedges and low red-brick walls, tall trees and grass verges at the north end.

Blenheim Road.note: Late Victorian/Edwardian villas and semis: red brick with buff or white dressings, several silver-grey Reading brick fronts with red-brick quoins, white bay windows and slate roofs; some Edwardian semis with mock-Tudor gables. A few 1970s-80s infill detached houses in orange brick. Low brick walls and hedges in front.

Oakley Road.note: Edwardian red-brick semis with dormers and tall chimneys mixed with later red-brick detached houses, behind low brick walls and hedges; only 3 of 6 views loaded.

St. Andrew's Road.note: Mixed road: large Victorian red-brick detached house with slate roof and white gables beside 1930s semis with rendered upper floors and later red-brick houses, behind hedges and low walls.

The Cloisters.note: The views only show the entrance off Priest Hill, screened by tall conifers and hedges; the only buildings visible are distant red-brick Edwardian houses on Priest Hill, so the close itself is unseen.

Knighton Close.note: A short terrace of 1960s/70s three-storey townhouses in buff brick with pale cladding on the upper floor and dormers in a brown tile roof; the other view is just a hedge and bank.

Victoria Road.note: Edwardian semis with red-brick ground floors and white-rendered upper floors, some with black-and-white timbered gables and tile roofs, behind low brick walls and hedges; the other view shows a school building on Hemdean Road.

Queen Street.note: Victorian two-storey red-brick terraces with slate roofs, small bays and low brick front walls, a white-rendered end house and a white-rendered Victorian cottage; at the western end some 1980s-2000s red-brick semis with gravel parking.

Orwell Close.note: 1960s-70s red-brick detached houses with white boarded upper panels and front porches, open-plan sloping lawns.

Dellwood Park.note: A leafy modern cul-de-sac of large red-brick detached houses with rendered or mock-Tudor timbered gables and bay windows among mature trees.

Chelford Way.note: 1960s/70s red-brick detached houses with white-framed windows, side carports and brown tile roofs behind lawns and shrubs; the other view is a building-site hoarding in front of a tile-hung chalet house under scaffolding.

Blagrave Farm Lane.note: A narrow, overgrown edge-of-town lane with only one house clearly seen, a white-rendered chalet house with a dark tile roof behind a timber fence; the rest is hedge and woodland.

Woodford Close.note: A 1960s-70s close of buff and orange brick detached houses with white panels around the windows and shallow roofs on open-plan lawns.

Woodcote Way.note: Plain red-brick bay-windowed semis from the 1930s-50s with hipped brown tiled roofs, behind low brick walls, hedges and fences with grass verges.

Conisboro Avenue.note: A long mixed road: Edwardian red-brick houses with rendered upper floors at the south end, later detached infill and 1970s orange-brick houses further north, mostly behind tall hedges and brick walls.

Queensborough Drive.note: 1960s-70s estate houses in red brick with white boarded or rendered upper floors, shallow roofs and attached garages on open-plan fronts.

Fernbrook Road.note: Red-brick 1930s-50s semis with two-storey bay windows and hipped brown tiled roofs behind picket fences and hedges, with grass verges and big conifers; the east end is hidden by hedges.

Westdene Crescent.note: Red-brick bungalows and chalet bungalows with steep brown tiled roofs and dormers, low brick walls, around a grassed island.

Lawson Drive.note: From Conisboro Avenue at the junction: 1930s red-brick semis with white-rendered bays and gables and hipped dark tile roofs behind hedges and low brick walls; Lawson Drive itself is not directly seen.

Atterbury Gardens.note: From the Woodford Close end: 1980s red-brick and buff-brick detached houses with brown tile roofs and open drives; the gated entrance and brick piers to Atterbury Gardens itself are hidden by trees.

Wincroft Road.note: Bungalows and modest detached houses glimpsed behind tall fences and hedges, red brick with brown tiled roofs, with wide grass verges.

Geoffreyson Road.note: Red-brick semis from the 1930s-50s, some with bay windows, brown and dark tiled roofs, fences and hedges in front and grass verges.

Pinewood Drive.note: Narrow tree-lined drive; one modern orange-brick detached house with a bay window and an older red-brick house in the distance were all that showed past conifers and hedges.

Regency Heights.note: From the Woodford Close end: 1960s/70s link-detached houses in red/buff brick with dark-stained timber and white-boarded upper panels and balconies, low-pitched tile roofs, open-plan fronts; a short drive leads to newer red-brick gabled houses (Regency Heights proper) in the distance.

Conisboro Way.note: 2012 imagery: postwar red-brick semis/short terraces with brown tile roofs and open lawns behind wide grass verges; the other view is a blurred site cabin on a corner plot.

Gurney Close.note: A cul-de-sac of 1960s red and orange brick bungalows and a few chalet bungalows with brown concrete tile roofs behind low brick walls.

Gurney Drive.note: 1960s brick bungalows with brown concrete tile roofs, some with white weatherboard gables and attached garages, on open-plan drives and lawns.

Crispin Close.note: 1960s-70s close of plain detached red and brown brick houses with shallow brown roofs, some dark panels between windows, attached garages and open lawns.

Shepherds Lane.note: A through lane with grass verges where mixed-age detached houses and chalet bungalows, some white rendered and some newer orange brick, sit well back behind tall hedges and fences.

The Grange.note: 1990s executive estate of large detached red-brick houses with double garages, front gables that are tile-hung or pale rendered, brown tiled roofs and open lawns with shrubs.

Hilltop Road.note: Plain postwar red-brick semis with bay windows and brown tiled roofs behind low fences and verges, ending in a turning circle with a few later brick detached houses.

Tokers Green Lane.note: 1990s executive estate of large detached red-brick houses with double garages, front gables that are tile-hung or pale rendered, brown tiled roofs and open lawns with shrubs.

Morecambe Avenue.note: 1930s red-brick semis with two-storey bay windows under small tile-hung gables, behind low walls and hedges on a verge-lined street.

Silverthorne Drive.note: 1960s estate of semis and detached houses with brick ground floors and white or cream boarded/rendered uppers, plus buff-brick chalet bungalows with big dormers at the west end; mostly open lawns with a few hedges.

Sandcroft Road.note: 1960s-70s detached houses with dark tile-hung or boarded upper floors over brick, and white-rendered houses, behind short hedges.

Carlton Road.note: 1960s-70s estate houses with shallow gables facing the road, white render or orange brick below and dark tile-hung or boarded upper floors, on open-plan lawns.

Haldane Road.note: A road of postwar bungalows with low brown-tiled hipped roofs behind low brick walls, hedges and fences, with grassy corners at the junctions.

Saint David's Close.note: 1960s-70s close of chalet-style semis and detached houses with steep brown tiled roofs sweeping down over the ground floor, brick below and white boarding above, with open front gardens.

Uplands Road.note: Mostly side and back garden fences on the stretches seen, with red-brick interwar semis and detached houses under hipped tiled roofs, a red-roofed chalet bungalow and a white rendered house.

Ashcroft Close.note: A 1960s-70s close of brick detached houses with shallow front gables and dark tile-hung upper floors, behind low brick walls, hedges and fences.

Lymington Gate.note: 1960s red-brick bungalows with brown concrete tile roofs and white uPVC windows behind low red-brick walls, with a few two-storey houses and pitched-roof garages.

Kelvedon Way.note: Street of 1950s-60s red-brick bungalows with hipped brown tiled roofs, small front bays and side garages, behind low brick walls, some topped with pierced concrete blocks.

Tyler Close.note: 1960s-70s close with buff-brick garages and screen-block walls; houses mostly hidden.

Wrenfield Drive.note: Postwar red-brick semis with hipped roofs stepping up a hillside above the road, with a long fenced verge with young trees on the other side.

Hunters Chase.note: A modern estate spine road lined mostly by hedges, fences and garden walls, with red and orange brick 1990s detached houses glimpsed side-on.

Tymawr.note: 1990s estate of buff-brick detached houses with bay windows, some dark tile-hung gables and attached garages, plus a red-brick terrace; open drives and tiny front gardens.

Brill Close.note: Mix of 1960s-70s bungalows and chalet bungalows in orange brick with white boarding, and 1980s-90s red-brick detached houses with dark brown tile roofs, tile-hung bays and integral garages; open-plan fronts and paved drives, hedges and fences on the lower section.

Glyncastle.note: Late-1980s/90s detached houses in buff or red brick with red tile-hung gables, integral garages and open front lawns; one side of the road is just hedge and trees.

Sheridan Avenue.note: A 1950s hillside street of red-brick semis mixed with red-brick bungalows, brown tiled roofs, low brick front walls with hedges and grass verges.

Ammanford.note: 1990s red-brick houses with small tiled porches and bay windows, some stepped up the slope above brick retaining walls; only two views so few houses seen.

Charlotte Close.note: Small 2000s close of large red-brick houses with cream rendered gables and stone-look window heads behind low brick walls with railings and hedges; an older white rendered mock-Tudor house stands at the entrance.

Blaenavon.note: Modern red-brick detached houses with gables and garages; one usable view.

Kidmore Court.note: 1990s/2000s red-brick detached houses with dark tile roofs, small canopy porches and integral garages, behind small lawns and shrubs; the other view (2012 imagery) is a conifer hedge.

Woodberry Close.note: 1930s-style semis in red brick with white-rendered two-storey bays and gables, arched porches and hipped brown tile roofs, behind low brick walls and paved drives - same builder as Valley Close.

Valley Close.note: 1930s-style semis in red brick with white-rendered two-storey bay windows and gables, arched porches and hipped dark tile roofs, behind low brick walls with paved and lawned drives.

Midsummer Meadow.note: 1990s red-brick detached houses with red-brown tile-hung upper gables on open corner lawns, woodland edge.

Winterberry Way.note: Late-1980s/90s estate of detached buff and red brick houses with front gables, some red tile-hung or dark-boarded uppers, garages and a few bungalows, on open fronts with shrubs and hedges.

Bramblings.note: 1980s houses in orange-red brick with tile-hung upper floors (and some black weatherboarding), steep dark-brown tile roofs with dormers and catslide garages, open-plan front lawns.

Mardy.note: 1990s/2000s red-brick detached houses with dark tile roofs, small canopy porches and integral garages, behind small lawns and shrubs; the other view (2012 imagery) is a conifer hedge.

Gravel Hill.note: old village cottages (Kidmore End Road, Emmer Green, Lower Caversham lanes)

Badgers Rise.note: 1980s estate of small detached and semi houses and link garages in red and buff brick with brown concrete tile roofs, open lawns and drives, wooded hillside behind.

Blaenant.note: 1990s hillside estate: buff or red brick detached houses with cream rendered uppers, and a stepped terrace of three-storey townhouses with garages below and railinged steps up to the doors.

Morlais.note: 1980s-90s estate of red-brick detached houses with white-painted gables and integral garages on open-plan lawns, plus a stepped row of townhouses up the slope.

Treforgan.note: 1990s detached red-brick houses with front gables, bay windows and integral garages on open plots; the other side of the road is a thick hedge bank; only two views.

Briar Close.note: 1960s hillside close of red-brick detached houses with white-panelled or rendered gable fronts and red-brick bungalows, brown tile roofs, open lawns and steep drives, wooded hill behind.

Rotherfield Way.note: Southern end has 1930s semis and detached houses with red brick ground floors and white-rendered upper floors under red/brown tile hipped roofs; further north 1960s-70s detached houses and chalet bungalows in buff/orange brick with white boarding, behind hedges and big trees.

Grove Hill.note: Most views are tall hedges and trees; the houses glimpsed are detached chalet bungalows and 1960s-70s houses with white render and dormers or orange/red brick, under brown or dark tile roofs, plus a few older red-brick houses.

Tredegar Road.note: A hillside road with long green gaps of trees and scrub, and a stepped row of white-rendered and brick houses with orange roofs at the southern end.

Glenrhondda.note: 1990s red-brick detached houses, several with black-and-white mock-Tudor gables, block-paved drives and open lawns.

Tylorstown.note: A 1990s cul-de-sac of red-brick detached houses with dormers and gabled porches on open lawns, screened from the road by hedges.

Cwmcarn.note: 1990s red-brick detached houses, several with black-and-white mock-Tudor gables, block-paved drives and open lawns.

Rhigos.note: 1990s detached red-brick houses with bay windows, small decorative timber trusses in the gables, attached garages and open front lawns.

one way.note: 1980s-90s estate of red-brick detached houses with white-painted gables and integral garages on open-plan lawns, plus a stepped row of townhouses up the slope.

Aberaman.note: A 1990s cul-de-sac of red and orange brick detached executive houses with bay windows, small gables and integral garages on open-plan plots with a few hedges.

Hafod.note: Modern red-brick detached houses with gabled porches and garages on open lawns; only one view loaded.

Penn Close.note: Houses largely hidden by tall hedges; visible ones are buff and red brick postwar semis with chimneys.

Surley Row.note: Very leafy: many views are mostly trees, hedges and old high brick garden walls. Older white-rendered Georgian/Victorian houses near the south end, then 1960s-80s and modern detached houses in brown/orange brick, plus some postwar semis on open lawns.

Merthyr Vale.note: old village cottages (Kidmore End Road, Emmer Green, Lower Caversham lanes)

Cherwell Road.note: Houses largely hidden by tall hedges; visible ones are buff and red brick postwar semis with chimneys.

Emmer Green, Reading,.note: Few houses visible: the road runs past a recreation ground/green with mature trees, a Victorian red-brick school or chapel with arched windows, a modern buff-brick community building, a block of lock-up garages and a 1960s three-storey red-brick terrace or flats beyond.

Chiltern Court.note: 1980s detached houses with dormers and bungalows, all red brick with brown concrete tile roofs, integral garages and open lawns; mature trees around.

Grove Road.note: Few houses visible: the road runs past a recreation ground/green with mature trees, a Victorian red-brick school or chapel with arched windows, a modern buff-brick community building, a block of lock-up garages and a 1960s three-storey red-brick terrace or flats beyond.

Lyefield Court.note: 1990s red-brick gabled houses behind a brick boundary wall and timber fences, with large trees.

Highdown Hill Road.note: 1930s red-brick semis and detached houses with hipped dark tile roofs, bay windows and tile-hung or rendered gables, behind hedges and gravel drives off wide grass verges; the top end is a wooded hillside lane with scattered modern rendered houses.

Albany Gardens.note: Only the junction is visible: interwar white-rendered and red-brick semis behind low brick walls and wide grass verges with big trees.

Highdown Avenue.note: Only one viewpoint loaded; red brick detached houses and a dark-roofed bungalow mostly hidden behind tall hedges and fences.

Eliot Close.note: Only one useful view: 1960s-70s two-storey terraces in red-brown brick with white panels under the windows, shallow brown-tile roofs, concrete-panel and close-board fences and small front gardens; the other view is a grassy green and trees.

Scott Close.note: 1970s estate of plain two-storey terraces in orange-brown and buff brick with shallow brown concrete-tile roofs and flat porch canopies, plus a few bungalows; open-plan lawns, paths and timber fences, backing onto woodland.

St Barnabas Road.note: 1960s-70s estates (Emmer Green, Caversham Park Village): pale brick, tile-hung or boarded upper fronts, concrete tiles

Eric Avenue.note: Mostly detached red-brick bungalows and chalet bungalows with gabled or hipped tile roofs behind low red-brick walls and hedges, with a few modern red-brick detached houses near the Gorselands end; corner plots show long fenced gardens.

Soane End.note: Only one viewpoint loaded; red brick detached houses and a dark-roofed bungalow mostly hidden behind tall hedges and fences.

Old Barn Close.note: Mostly detached red-brick bungalows and chalet bungalows with gabled or hipped tile roofs behind low red-brick walls and hedges, with a few modern red-brick detached houses near the Gorselands end; corner plots show long fenced gardens.

Barnes Road.note: 1990s red-brick gabled houses behind a brick boundary wall and timber fences, with large trees.

Chaucer Close.note: 1970s estate of plain two-storey terraces and end houses in orange-brown brick with brown or grey concrete tile roofs, mostly seen gable-end on behind a parking court and a block of lock-up garages.

Surley Place.note: Only distant views: red-brick 1980s/90s houses with dark tile roofs and white-boarded gables beyond the junction, retaining walls and a garage block; the place itself is barely visible.

Gorselands.note: 1980s detached houses with dormers and bungalows, all red brick with brown concrete tile roofs, integral garages and open lawns; mature trees around.

Bell Court.note: 1990s red-brick gabled houses behind a brick boundary wall and timber fences, with large trees.

Stuart Close.note: Postwar semis in red brick, many with cream/buff rendered upper floors, under hipped brown or dark tile roofs, plus a few bungalows; fronts are a mix of hedges, low brick walls, fences and paved drives, with grass verges.

Southdown Road.note: Postwar hipped-roof semis with red-brick ground floors and cream-rendered upper floors, brown tile roofs, set up on grassy banks with hedges; one view is just woodland.

Evesham Road.note: Late-1940s/50s semis with red brick ground floors and pebbledash or cream render above, hipped brown/dark tile roofs and chimneys, set back behind privet hedges, low fences and wide grass greens with mature trees.

Bellingham Walk.note: 1960s-70s two-storey terraces in buff/orange brick with brown tile-hung or boarded upper fronts, seen from behind over fences and garage courts; very leafy edges.

Grove Cottages.note: 1960s-70s estates (Emmer Green, Caversham Park Village): pale brick, tile-hung or boarded upper fronts, concrete tiles

The Gardeners.note: A recent (2010s) development of red-brick detached and semi houses with orange-red tile roofs and white gable boards, set behind post-and-rail fences off Surley Row.

Balmore Park.note: 1980s-90s estate of detached houses and a few semis in red and orange-brown brick under brown or dark plain-tile roofs, some with white-rendered first floors, porch canopies and integral garages; open-plan lawns and set in mature woodland.

Newlands Avenue.note: Interwar semis and bungalows in red brick, some with white-rendered upper floors and bay windows, behind low brick walls; a long stretch of tall fence and hedge on one side.

Berrylands Road.note: 1950s semis in red and orange-red brick with hipped or gabled brown/dark tile roofs and side garages, plus several white-rendered semis and a few detached houses; fronts of low brick walls, close-board fences and hedges, many paved drives.

The Ridgeway.note: 1960s semis in red brick with white-painted boarded or rendered panels on the upper floor, integral garages and brown/dark tile roofs, set behind open lawns and drives; wide grass verges and mature trees, a wooded bank at one end.

Buckingham Drive.note: Postwar council-built estate: semis and short terraces in red brick, many with cream-rendered or panelled upper floors (one terrace has green-painted upper panels), hipped brown tile roofs, and three-storey brown-brick flat blocks set back behind big greens. Two of the three panoramas date from 2012.

Knights Way.note: Post-war council estate: hipped-roof semis and short terraces, some all red brick, others with cream/buff render or pebbledash (often over a red-brick plinth or ground floor), low brick walls and hedges, plus 1960s four-storey red-brick flat blocks with blue panels round a car park.

Kidmore End Road.note: Mixed road: Victorian red-brick and rendered cottages/terraces at the southern end by the pub, then interwar and later detached and semi houses (many white-rendered) set back behind tall hedges, flint walls and trees further north.

Caversham Park Drive.note: Only the Peppard Road end (black railings, big trees, hedges) and a photosphere of the Caversham Park mansion (pale stone, columned) loaded; no houses on the drive itself were seen.

Oak Grove.note: Post-war council estate: hipped-roof semis and short terraces, some all red brick, others with cream/buff render or pebbledash (often over a red-brick plinth or ground floor), low brick walls and hedges, plus 1960s four-storey red-brick flat blocks with blue panels round a car park.

Balmore Drive.note: 1920s-30s semis: brick below, render above, hipped plain-tile roofs, bays, hedges

Picton Way.note: 1970s-80s executive estate of detached houses in orange-brown brick with brown concrete tile roofs, integral garages and some tile-hung or boarded panels, set behind open-plan lawns and block-paved drives among mature trees.

Sheepwalk.note: Hillside 1960s/70s chalet bungalows and detached houses in red brick with brown tile roofs and box dormers, raised gardens behind red-brick retaining walls.

Springfield Mews.note: 1990s/2000s detached houses with red-brick ground floors and white-rendered gables with arched windows and dark tile roofs, behind low brick walls with railings; down a side drive is an older white-rendered villa.

St Lukes Way.note: A long two-storey 1990s red-brick care home with a hipped dark tile roof set in lawns and a car park, and a red-brick flats block behind tall clipped conifer hedges.

Buckingham Gate.note: 1980s/90s red-brick detached houses with attached garages and brown tile roofs among dense hedges and trees; one of two views is just hedge.

Greycoat Court.note: 1920s-30s semis: brick below, render above, hipped plain-tile roofs, bays, hedges

Field View.note: 1920s-30s semis: brick below, render above, hipped plain-tile roofs, bays, hedges

Marshland Square.note: Postwar hipped-roof semis with red brick ground floors and cream/white rendered upper floors, brown tile roofs, behind tall privet hedges; two of four views are just trees and shrubs.

Hare Warren Court.note: 1990s/2000s three-storey red-brick flats with cream-rendered top floors, small balconies and dormers, around a block-paved car court, plus a red-brick gabled house and a timber bin store.

Derby Road.note: 1920s-30s semis: brick below, render above, hipped plain-tile roofs, bays, hedges

Grosvenor Road.note: 1920s-30s semis: brick below, render above, hipped plain-tile roofs, bays, hedges

St Lukes Court.note: A long two-storey 1990s red-brick care home with a hipped dark tile roof set in lawns and a car park, and a red-brick flats block behind tall clipped conifer hedges.

Notley Place.note: A mix: four-storey 1960s red-brick council flats with blue window panels set in lawns, 1980s/90s red-brick houses and a small hipped-roof flats block, and postwar semis behind picket fences further along.

Michaels Chase.note: 1920s-30s semis: brick below, render above, hipped plain-tile roofs, bays, hedges

Chiltern Road.note: 1930s semis with hipped tiled roofs and bays: red brick ground floors with white or cream rendered upper floors, some fully rendered, a few with mock-Tudor gables; low brick walls and hedges, wide grass verges with trees, and a newer red-brick house at the north end.

Greystoke Road.note: A large white-rendered Regency/Victorian villa with a columned porch behind a clipped hedge, plus a red-brick garage block; heavily treed and only two views.
